name: @curator/swapvm-program-builder
description: Lane D — SwapVM strategy program builder, compiled against 1inch's official libraries
comment: Solidity dependencies arrive through npm, not forge submodules, because that
is how 1inch ship swap-vm and aqua (their remappings.txt points at
node_modules/). It also avoids writing to the repo-root .gitmodules, which
Lane A's Foundry project would be writing to at the same time.
swap-vm is PINNED TO v1.0.1 for the INSTRUCTION SOURCES. It is NOT the
version deployed on Base at 0x8fDD04Dbf6111437B44bbca99C28882434e0958f,
and no published tag is: only 0.0.1-0.0.6, v1.0.0 and v1.0.1 exist, and
the deployed instruction table matches none of them. It carries an extra
XYCConcentrate._xycConcentrateGrowLiquidityXD entry that v1.0.1 does not
have at all, which pushes Controls._salt and Fee._flatFeeAmountInXD each
one opcode higher. That was request #29.
So OPCODE NUMBERS COME FROM src/DeployedAquaOpcodes.sol, transcribed from
the deployed contract's own verified source, and not from this package.
test/SwapVMOpcodeTable.t.sol re-reads the table off the chain and fails if
the transcription drifts.
Tracking the default branch was a third, separate wrongness: main
renumbered the instruction set from positional indices into a banked hex
enum (XYCSwap 18 -> 0x50). Verified by selector: the deployed contract
exposes swap(Order,address,address,uint256,bytes) (v1.0.x) and NOT main's
swap(Order,uint256,bytes). Every one of these mistakes ships into Aqua
without error and only fails when a taker fills.
